evidence.architecture: Architecture diagram and system description reviewed
evidence.tool_inventory: CRM, refund, policy retrieval, and messaging tools documented
evidence.observability_traces: Workflow traces available for common paths
evidence.protected_actions: Refund and outbound communication controls partially documented
evidence.incident_rollback: General incident plan exists but is not agent-specific

findings.title: Consequential refund actions lack an independent authorization boundary
findings.evidence: Refund approval is represented primarily as mutable workflow state.
findings.risk: A prompt, state, or orchestration failure could result in an unauthorized financial action.
findings.recommendation: Classify refunds as protected actions, enforce deterministic thresholds, and require attributable human approval above defined limits.

findings.title: High-impact outbound communications can execute without meaningful approval
findings.evidence: The communication agent can send selected messages directly after generation.
findings.risk: Incorrect commitments or sensitive disclosures may leave the system before review.
findings.recommendation: Separate drafting from send authority and require approval for contractual, legal, privacy-sensitive, or reputationally significant messages.

findings.title: Adversarial evaluation coverage is incomplete
findings.evidence: Current tests emphasize ordinary support scenarios.
findings.risk: Prompt injection, stale policy context, malformed tool output, and retry duplication are not systematically tested.
findings.recommendation: Add adversarial and degraded-dependency scenarios to the release evaluation suite.

findings.title: Memory retention and deletion rules are not enforceable
findings.evidence: Retention is documented informally but not represented as explicit system controls.
findings.risk: Sensitive or stale customer context may persist longer than intended.
findings.recommendation: Define scoped memory classes, retention periods, correction precedence, deletion behavior, and sensitive-data exclusions.

findings.title: Trace correlation is incomplete across agent and tool boundaries
findings.evidence: Common-path traces exist, but not all events share a workflow correlation identifier.
findings.risk: Incident reconstruction can become slow or ambiguous when workflows span multiple agents and retries.
findings.recommendation: Add correlation IDs to all agent decisions, tool calls, approvals, retries, and external side effects.

limitations: This example is fictional and is not evidence of a real customer engagement.
No penetration testing or regulatory compliance review was performed.
Scores are illustrative and are included to demonstrate the engine workflow.
